title: When someone is unkind
hook: a stranger on a late train tells a woman born in her city that she doesn't belong; the raised hand on the murtis
carry: your worth isn't up for a vote
tomorrow: The first mountain, from the top

segments.voice: Yesterday, nazar: a thread on a wrist and a dot on a cheek. Your line was someone was looking out for you. Today, the harder question: when the look isn't kind. Day three hundred twenty-nine.

She was born in this city. She went to school here, works here, loves it. One evening on a late train, a stranger tells her she doesn't really belong here, and throws in a slur meant for a religion that isn't even hers. Then he gets off at the next stop. She sits there shaking, the train still moving, everyone looking at their phones. A lot of people know a version of that night. This week has been about neighbors. Today, the hard part: when a neighbor isn't kind.
screen: `A LATE TRAIN.` → `YOU DON'T BELONG HERE.` → `WHEN A NEIGHBOR ISN'T KIND.`

segments.voice: Start with something you can see on almost any shrine. Look at Ganesha, or Durga, or Vishnu. One hand is often raised, palm out, fingers up. That's the abhaya mudra. Abhaya means no fear. The gesture says: don't be afraid. Here's what the tradition puts in that hand. First, your worth isn't up for a vote. You met the atman on day ten: someone is in there. In the Gita, Krishna says weapons can't cut it and fire can't burn it. A stranger's words can shake you. They can't reach that. Second, dignity, not hate. Ahimsa, from day seventeen, means not harming, and that includes not answering cruelty with more cruelty. It never means staying silent or staying unsafe. Move away. Tell someone. Report it. Ask for help. Third, pride without a ladder. You can love your festivals, your food, your temples, your grandmother's songs, without claiming anyone else's are lower. One truth, many names asks exactly that. And fourth, you're not alone. Lean on your people. If you're ever in danger, call local emergency services. If a night like that leaves you somewhere dark, in the US you can call or text 988, any hour, and talk to someone; elsewhere, local emergency help is there too. This week you visited five other houses and heard each in its own words. The bow from day four still holds, even when someone doesn't bow back: the light in me sees the light in you.
screen: `ABHAYA — DON'T BE AFRAID.` · `YOUR WORTH ISN'T UP FOR A VOTE.` · `DIGNITY, NOT HATE.` · `YOU'RE NOT ALONE.`

segments.voice: If you like, lift your right hand, palm out, the way the murtis do, and name a moment someone made you feel small, without reliving it. Breathe in slowly, and on the out-breath let the hand say what it says: don't be afraid. If you pray, you can ask for courage; if you don't, let the steady breath be the answer. Lower your hand when you're ready.
Abhaya mudra. The raised open palm on so many murtis: no fear, don't be afraid. Today's word.
Your line: your worth isn't up for a vote. Nobody on a train gets to decide it. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 329 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE FIRST MOUNTAIN, FROM THE TOP.`
